plain_english_title: Respiratory System Guide: Burn Pit Asthma/Sinusitis/Rhinitis, Sleep Apnea CPAP Rules & Coexisting Lung Ratings
what_this_means: With PACT Act burn-pit presumptions (38 U.S.C. § 1120; 38 C.F.R. § 3.320) making asthma, chronic rhinitis, chronic sinusitis, COPD, interstitial lung disease, sarcoidosis, and respiratory cancers presumptive for covered Gulf War and post-9/11 Veterans, accurate evaluation under 38 C.F.R. §§ 4.96–4.97 matters more than ever. This comparison explains how VA evaluates PFT breathing numbers vs. inhaler/steroid therapy, why nasal polyps on CT or endoscopy establish 30% under Diagnostic Code 6522 Rhinitis, why upper-airway nose/sinus ratings stack separately with lower-lung ratings, and how Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) interacts with coexisting lung disease.
record_clues: A Rating Code Sheet subsuming Chronic Sinusitis (Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514) or Allergic Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) into Asthma (Diagnostic Code 6602) or Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847).
Allergic or Vasomotor Rhinitis (Diagnostic Code 6522) rated at 0% or 10% despite a sinus CT scan or ENT nasal endoscopy documenting nasal polyps (which warrants 30%).
Obstructive Sleep Apnea (Diagnostic Code 6847) rated below 50% despite a medical prescription for a CPAP, BiPAP, APAP, or oral mandibular-advancement breathing assistance device.

Total laryngectomy (Diagnostic Code 6518) or complete organic aphonia / loss of speech (Diagnostic Code 6519) rated 100% without concurrent statutory Special Monthly Compensation (SMC(k) under 38 C.F.R. § 3.350(a)(6)).
important_cautions: Endoscopic sinus surgery vs. 'radical surgery': routine functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS), polypectomy, or turbinate reduction generally counts as 'repeated surgeries' rather than 'radical surgery' (open obliterative procedures like Caldwell-Luc) under Diagnostic Codes 6510–6514.

Medication rules differ by code: because Diagnostic Code 6602 (Asthma) explicitly builds bronchodilator and corticosteroid medication into its 10%, 30%, 60%, and 100% tiers, it follows its explicit medication text (McCarroll v. McDonald), whereas non-medication codes like Sinusitis or Rhinitis cannot be discounted for temporary medication relief (Ingram v. Collins).

Do not confuse proposed or rescinded rules with active law: RIN 2900-AQ72 (87 FR 8474 & 89 FR 74162, proposing revised sleep apnea CPAP rules and Diagnostic Code 6605 constrictive bronchiolitis) remains a proposed, unfinalized rule (not enacted law), and VA's February 17, 2026 § 4.10 medication rule (91 FR 7118) was formally rescinded on February 27, 2026 (91 FR 9712).

Pre-October 7, 1996 decisions used older qualitative lung criteria rather than Diagnostic Code 6847 or modern PFT tables, and 38 C.F.R. § 20.1409(c) limits Board Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) review to one final merits decision per prior Board issue.
questions_for_representative: Have my Sinusitis (antibiotic courses / incapacitating episodes), Rhinitis (nasal polyps or >50% nasal blockage), and Asthma/COPD/Sleep Apnea all been evaluated under their distinct upper- vs. lower-respiratory rules?
Does a sinus CT scan or ENT exam show nasal polyps warranting 30% under Diagnostic Code 6522?

If I have constrictive bronchiolitis or burn-pit lung injury with normal spirometry (FEV-1) but abnormal diffusing capacity (DLCO) or exercise limitation, did the examiner address DLCO under 38 C.F.R. § 4.96(d)?
If both Asthma and Sleep Apnea are service-connected, did VA consider elevating the single lower-respiratory rating to 60% or 100% under § 4.96(a) (Urban v. Shulkin)?
